Subject: VAT question on platform fee / reseller billing

Hi Karthik,

Quick one — we received Redwood invoice #12345 for platform fees (Jan-Feb usage) but our UK reseller, ResellCo, is handling customer billing in the channel. AP is asking whether Redwood should charge UK VAT on the platform portion, or whether the reverse-charge should apply to ResellCo.

Attached is our PO and ResellCo's reseller agreement (they asked us to check with you). Can you confirm:
- Should Redwood invoice ProTech with VAT?
- If reverse-charge applies, do you need a VAT ID from ResellCo or is ProTech's VAT-exempt status sufficient?

We need to clear this before payment runs next week.

Thanks,

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the note and the docs. A few clarifying Qs as I loop finance/tax:

1) Who is the contractual buyer on our invoice currently — ProTech or ResellCo? (I think ProTech, per PO, but want to confirm.)
2) Is ResellCo registered for UK VAT and will they be the B2B recipient of the platform service for resale?

Tentative guidance: if ProTech is the contracted buyer and is UK-established and not VAT-registered for the supply, we typically charge UK VAT. If the immediate customer is a UK VAT-registered business (ResellCo) and the supply is for resale, reverse-charge can apply, but we need ResellCo's VAT number and a statement on the invoice ("reverse charge - VAT to be accounted for by the customer").

Laura / Marissa — can you confirm Redwood's standard treatment for platform licensing fees when a channel partner invoices the end-customer? Also, do we require the reseller to be named on our invoice to apply reverse-charge, or is a reseller-managed split allowed with a split invoice?

Karthik

Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VAT question on platform fee / reseller billing

Hi all — looping in tax ops guidance from our UK compliance notes. Short answer: we can support reverse-charge treatment but need the following in place:

- Invoice must be raised to the VAT-registered UK business that is the recipient of the supply (ResellCo) OR the invoice must clearly state that the supply is B2B and include the VAT registration number of the recipient if ProTech asks us to invoice ProTech but claim reverse-charge (this is less common).
- We require a formal VAT number for the recipient (ResellCo) and a note on the invoice: "Reverse charge - VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Art. 194 VAT Directive". For UK, use the domestic phrasing: "Reverse charge — customer to account for VAT under UK domestic reverse charge rules."
- If ProTech is paying on behalf of ResellCo (AP convenience), our accounting needs a written confirmation from ResellCo that they are the economic recipient for the service; otherwise we treat ProTech as the taxable supply.

Operational options we can support:
A) Re-issue invoice to ResellCo (preferred): Redwood invoices ResellCo (no VAT charged if we have their UK VAT number and reverse-charge indicated). ProTech pays ResellCo separately.
B) Split invoice: Redwood issues two line items on one invoice — platform fee (invoiced net with reverse-charge to ResellCo) and value-added professional services (if any) billed to ProTech with VAT as applicable. This requires a reseller nomination email from ResellCo and their VAT number.

We can re-issue the existing invoice to implement A or B. Marissa — can you prepare a re-issued invoice template (reverse-charge phrasing) and a CSV that maps the split by line if they pick option B?

Laura
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
